title: Solve a bare quadratic
subtitle: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables  · 33 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **33 of the official questions in Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables  are this one** — 10 Easy, 16 Medium, 7 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- It's a single equation with an x^2 term and no unknown constants.
- The question asks for 'a solution', 'the positive solution' or 'what values satisfy', and the choices are specific numbers, sometimes pairs with radicals.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) If there's no x term, isolate x^2 and take ± the square root.
- 2) Otherwise, get it into standard form and factor.
- If it doesn't factor cleanly, or the choices contain radicals, use the quadratic formula.
- 3) Pick the root the question asks for, such as the positive one.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Graph y = left side - right side, or type both sides as separate curves, and click the x-intercepts or intersection points.
This is fastest when the roots are ugly radicals: match the decimals to the choices.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You forget the negative root, or you take the square root before isolating x^2.
The wrong choices are usually the positive root of a nearby equation with a sign flipped or a coefficient left undivided.

sections.heading: You are losing these
